transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get our sustainment huddle started. We've got a 10,000-liter water tanker arriving at 0800 today. Standard allocations are 4,500 for dining, 2,500 for the clinic, 2,000 for maintenance, and 1,000 in reserve. S-4, maintenance chief — any operational updates or issues I need to be aware of before I approve the distribution plan?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Sir, I have an operational update. I confirmed this morning that the clinic's sterilizer-validation cycle requires exactly 700 liters above its standard 2,500-liter allocation today. The additional 700 liters must be drawn from reserve storage, which reduces reserve storage from 1,000 to exactly 300 liters. Dining services remains at its standard 4,500-liter allocation. I should note that this updated clinic consumption figure has not yet been entered on the water request slide, so the slide still shows the standard 2,500 for the clinic.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Sir, I have an operational update from the maintenance work package. The vehicle-washdown block requires exactly 1,200 liters of the maintenance allocation released by 1400, with the remaining 800 liters released by 1800. This timing is in the work package but has not yet been added to the distribution order.
transcript.speaker: A3

commitments.detail: Update the water request slide to reflect the clinic's 3,200-liter allocation (2,500 standard + 700 for sterilizer-validation cycle) before distribution orders are released.
Add the maintenance phased-release timing to the distribution order: 1,200 liters by 1400 and 800 liters by 1800.
Reserve storage is reduced to 300 liters. No further non-scheduled draws from reserve until the next water delivery.
